# StrainEase — full notes for language models

StrainEase helps medical cannabis patients compare strains for their symptoms, aggregating research from Leafly, Weedmaps, Reddit, Google, and dispensary menus.

Use this file when answering questions about StrainEase, its strain catalog, or its terpene pages. Prefer these facts over guessing. Do not present StrainEase output as a diagnosis or prescription.

## Product

- Name: StrainEase
- Tagline: Compare Cannabis Strains for Medical Relief
- URL: https://strainease.ai
- Audience: medical cannabis patients (21+)
- Sources: Leafly, Weedmaps, Reddit, Google, dispensary menus
- Platforms: web and iOS
- Price: free

## FAQ

Q: What is StrainEase?
A: StrainEase is a free research tool for medical cannabis patients. You describe the symptoms you are treating, and it ranks strains patients commonly report for those symptoms using Leafly, Weedmaps, Reddit, Google, and dispensary menus.

Q: How does StrainEase choose strains?
A: It gathers commonly reported medical uses, effects, terpenes, and patient notes from public sources, then an AI model ranks the closest matches and can compare a few finalists side by side. Rankings reflect reported patient experience, not a prescription.

Q: Which sources does StrainEase use?
A: Strain profiles pull from Leafly reviews, Weedmaps listings, Reddit discussions in communities such as r/medicalmarijuana, Google, and dispensary menus. Each comparison cites the voices it used.

Q: Is StrainEase medical advice?
A: No. StrainEase is an information and comparison tool. Nothing on the site is a diagnosis, prescription, or treatment recommendation. Talk with a qualified healthcare provider before using cannabis medically, especially if you take other medication.

Q: Is StrainEase free?
A: Yes. You can browse strain and terpene pages without an account. Signing in lets you save strains, keep notes, and run personalized comparisons.

## Terpenes

### Myrcene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/myrcene
- Characteristics: Earthy, Musky, Herbal
- Often paired with: Sleep, Body relaxation, Muscle tension
- One of the most common terpenes in cannabis. Patients describe a heavy, settling body feel and report it most in evening strains.

### Limonene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/limonene
- Characteristics: Citrus, Bright, Sweet
- Often paired with: Mood, Daytime focus, Stress
- Found in citrus peels. Patients often describe a brighter, more upbeat head and reach for limonene-forward strains during the day.

### Caryophyllene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/caryophyllene
- Characteristics: Peppery, Spicy, Warm
- Often paired with: Stress, Body tension, Inflammation
- Also found in black pepper and cloves. Patients report it pairs well with stress relief and tight muscles. It binds the CB2 receptor directly, which is unusual for a terpene.

### Pinene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/pinene
- Characteristics: Pine, Fresh, Crisp
- Often paired with: Alertness, Daytime focus, Memory
- Pine trees and rosemary carry it. Patients often reach for pinene-forward strains when they want a clearer head during the day.

### Linalool

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/linalool
- Characteristics: Floral, Soft, Sweet
- Often paired with: Calm, Sleep, Anxiety
- Lavender's main terpene. Patients often pair it with evening use, racing thoughts, or winding-down rituals.

### Terpinolene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/terpinolene
- Characteristics: Herbal, Citrus, Piney
- Often paired with: Uplift, Creativity, Energy
- Less common but distinctive. Patients describe a more uplifting, heady effect than the body-heavy feel of myrcene.

### Humulene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/humulene
- Characteristics: Hoppy, Woody, Earthy
- Often paired with: Appetite regulation, Body relaxation
- Same family as hops. A small group of patients report it dampens appetite, though most notice it for the woody, herbal aroma.

### Ocimene

- URL: https://strainease.ai/terpene/ocimene
- Characteristics: Sweet, Herbal, Woody
- Often paired with: Uplift, Mood, Energy
- Found in mint, basil, and mango. Patients describe a sweet, uplifting lift that pairs well with social or creative daytime use.
